item.description: Tender Notice - Preparation of the Detailed Technical Specification and the Development of the Software for the Unified Automated Information and Analytical System of the Central Election Commission of Ukraine (Phase I) International IDEA - The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance Tender Reference No: 2026-07-097 Assignment Name: Preparation of the Detailed Technical Specification and the development of the software for the Unified Automated Information and Analytical System of the Central Election Commission of Ukraine (Phase I) Project Name: U-VOTE (Ukrainians Voting: Organizing Trustworthy Elections) Deadline for Submissions: Proposals must be submitted on or before 23:59 (CET), 7 October 2026 . Late submissions will not be considered for evaluation. Address for Submissions: E-mail: tendersubmissions@idea.int This email address is set up with an auto-response to acknowledge emails received. If you do not receive an auto-reply, please send a text message prior to the submission deadline (NO CALLS; CALLS WILL NOT BE ANSWERED) to +46725375735. In your text message, please provide the following: Tender reference no. and title; Email address you used for submission; Date and time you sent your submission (e.g. 01 December 2021, 12:30 CET ); Please also send the above information to tender@idea.int before the deadline for submission. Format for Submissions: Proposal must be submitted by email. Technical and Financial proposals must be submitted in separate files and marked accordingly. Price should not be mentioned in the Technical Proposal. The following text should be put in the subject field of the email: Tender No. (2026-07-097) Technical and Financial Proposals – Do not open before 23:59 (CET), 7 October 2026. Email Address for Clarifications: E-mail: tender@idea.int Clarifications may be requested via e-mail no later than 23 September 2026 at the above email address. Note a response to a request for clarifications will be issued to all tenderers on our website http://www.idea.int/ . Therefore, tenderers are advised to check the website regularly during the process. Note : there are two different email addresses as outlined above, one to be used for Submission of your final proposal and the second one to be used for clarifications and other related correspondence. REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS Section 1 General Information 1.1 The International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA) is an intergovernmental organization established in 1995, with member states across all continents, which aims to support sustainable democracy world-wide and assist in the development of institutions and the culture of democracy. At the interface between research, fieldwork and the donor community, IDEA provides a forum for dialogue, builds networks of experts, develops training materials and provides strategic advice at international, regional and national level, cooperating with a range of organizations. 1.2 International IDEA now invites proposals from qualified bidders for the provision of software development services for the Unified Automated Information and Analytical System of the Central Election Commission of Ukraine. A detailed description of the assignment is provided in the Terms of Reference attached to this Request for Proposal. The Framework Agreement resulting from this procurement may, at International IDEA’s discretion, also be used for the development and implementation of subsequent phases of the System. The use of the Framework Agreement for any subsequent phase shall be optional and shall not constitute an obligation on the part of International IDEA to procure such subsequent services from the Framework Agreement holder. 1.3 Tentative timeframe: It is anticipated that the services will commence in October 2026 and will be completed according to the delivery schedule defined in the Terms of Reference (TOR) and agreed in the contract. Section 2 Preparation of Proposals Essential Requirements 2.1 Language: The official language for the proposal, contract, reports and any other documents in relation to the assignment is English. All documents for the CEC, as well as correspondence with the CEC, must also be provided in Ukrainian. 2.2 To be eligible for consideration, the bidder must demonstrate the following experience and capabilities: A. Legal and Organizational Eligibility The Bidder must be a legally registered entity with an established presence in Ukraine and hold all licences, permits, and government approvals required to perform the Services under this solicitation; The Bidder may engage subcontractors for the performance of specific parts of the Services. The total value of the Services to be performed by subcontractors shall not exceed 35% of the total Contract value. Any proposed subcontracting exceeding this threshold shall be clearly identified and justified in the proposal and shall be subject to the prior written approval of International IDEA and the CEC. The Bidder shall clearly identify all proposed subcontractors in its proposal, including the scope of Services and responsibilities assigned to each subcontractor. Each proposed subcontractor shall comply with all applicable legal, licensing, permitting and regulatory requirements relevant to the Services it will perform. Key experts may be provided by proposed subcontractors, provided that this is clearly identified in the proposal and their availability for the assignment is demonstrated. The Bidder shall remain fully responsible for the performance of the Contract, including the performance, acts and omissions of its subcontractors and any key experts provided them. Relevant Experience The Bidder must demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) software development projects of comparable scope, size, and complexity within the last five (5) years preceding the commencement of this procurement procedure. Where a referenced project is subject to confidentiality, security or classification restrictions that prevent the Bidder from providing the evidence listed below, the Bidder may provide alternative verifiable evidence sufficient to demonstrate the nature, scope, complexity and successful completion of the assignment. International IDEA reserves the right to request additional information and/or undertake appropriate verification of such experience; At least one (1) of the referenced projects must have been delivered for a public sector entity. Projects implemented for public sector entities in Ukraine or abroad, including international organizations and donor-funded projects, as well as comparable large-scale, high-security information systems delivered for the private sector (e.g. banking, telecommunications, or critical infrastructure), shall be considered; Compliance with this requirement shall be demonstrated by providing, for each referenced project, one or more of the following: a copy of the relevant contract; a client reference letter; an acceptance certificate (or equivalent evidence of successful completion); or a reference to a publicly available procurement record (e.g. Prozorro). In the case of a consortium or joint venture, the above qualification requirements may be satisfied cumulatively by the consortium members. The experience of declared subcontractors may also be taken into account, provided that the respective subcontractor will perform the relevant part of the Services. Advantage Criteria Experience in developing or modernizing electoral/election-related information systems, or other comparable large-scale, mission-critical public-sector information systems; Experience integrating information systems with Ukrainian state registries and interoperability platforms (e.g. Trembita, State Voter Register, Unified State Register); Demonstrated experience in developing or modernizing high-availability and/or mission critical information systems designed to operate under peak-load and/or unstable connectivity conditions. Capacity Statement The Bidder must demonstrate sufficient financial, technical, and managerial capacity, as well as the necessary facilities and organizational resources, to successfully perform the Services under this procurement; The Bidder's aggregate turnover for the last three (3) completed financial years shall not be less than UAH 50,000,000, supported by appropriate financial documentation. B. Personnel Qualifications and Expertise The Bidder shall propose a qualified multidisciplinary project team with demonstrated experience in software architecture, business analysis, software engineering, quality assurance, cybersecurity, system integration, and project management. The proposed team should include at a minimum, the following key roles: Project Manager; Solution/Software Architect; Business Analyst; Lead Software Developer; Quality Assurance Lead; The Bidder shall additionally demonstrate access to the specialist expertise required for the performance of the Services, including, where applicable, cybersecurity, DevOps/infrastructure, Linux systems engineering, system integration/API development, data architecture, UX/UI and technical documentation. The proposed key experts shall meet the following minimum qualification requirements Key Expert Minimum Qualification and Experience Project Manager At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience, including at least three (3) years of experience managing software development or implementation of projects of comparable scope and complexity. Solution/Software Architect At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience, including at least three (3) years in solution and/or software architecture for complex information systems. Business Analyst At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience, including demonstrated experience in business and requirements analysis for complex information systems. item.description: Vertaler en Conferentietolk (m/v) Moedertaal Nederlands Eureca Strasbourg, France KLAAR VOOR EEN NIEUWE UITDAGING? De Centrale Commissie voor de Rijnvaart (CCR) heeft sinds 1815 als belangrijkste taak het waarborgen van de veiligheid en de welvaart van de Rijnvaart . Deze internationale organisatie staat bekend om haar belangrijke rol in de binnenvaart en is actief op het snijvlak van technische, sociale en milieuvraagstukken. Het wervingsbureau Eureca zoekt voor deze organisatie een vertaler en conferentietolk (m/v) met Nederlands als moedertaal , ter versterking van het team van vertalers. Functie op basis van een tijdelijk contract (duur: 4 jaar) met zicht op omzetting naar een vast contract. Mooi kantoor in het hart van Straatsburg met de mogelijkheid tot gedeeltelijk thuiswerken . DE FUNCTIE DIE WIJ JE AANBIEDEN Je rapporteert aan de secretaris-generaal en maakt deel uit van het team van vertalers. Jouw taken omvatten: Het vertalen van redactionele, technische en soms politiek gevoelige teksten vanuit het Duits en het Frans naar het Nederlands , met inachtneming van deadlines, kwaliteitseisen en de geldende terminologie, waarbij je je werklast zelfstandig en flexibel indeelt; Het volgen van ontwikkelingen binnen de werkterreinen van de organisatie en van terminologische en taalkundige ontwikkelingen, en het actualiseren van vertaalgeheugens en woordenlijsten; Nauwe samenwerking met de auteurs over taalkundige en stilistische keuzes; Simultaan vertalen van het Duits naar het Nederlands en omgekeerd tijdens vergaderingen, werkgroepen en gesprekken met tolk die plaatsvinden op het hoofdkantoor van de organisatie; Voorbereiding van elke tolkopdracht: bestudering van de werkdocumenten, de agenda en videomateriaal, gericht terminologisch onderzoek. WAT DEZE FUNCTIE AANTREKKELIJK MAAKT Het opbouwen van specialistische expertise op technisch, politiek en sectoraal gebied; Goede begeleiding tijdens je inwerkperiode; Werken in een internationale, dynamische en stimulerende werkomgeving. JE BENT GESCHIKT VOOR DEZE FUNCTIE ALS Je bent afgestudeerd met een master in vertalen en conferentietolken en beheerst naast je moedertaal, het Nederlands, ook het Duits uitstekend. Een goede beheersing van het Frans (B2 – C1) is een pluspunt voor vertalingen naar het Nederlands; Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar ervaring in vertalen en tolken; Je bent georganiseerd, nauwgezet en werkt graag in teamverband. Maar bovenal heb je passie voor kwaliteit! UW VOORDELEN Een contract voor een periode van 4 jaar met de mogelijkheid tot omzetting in een contract voor onbepaalde tijd na afloop van deze 4 jaar; Een belastingvrij nettosalaris; Een goede ziektekosten- en pensioenverzekering; Een werkweek van 38 uur, met de mogelijkheid om 2 dagen per week thuis te werken, en 30 vakantiedagen per jaar. Solliciteer door je cv en motivatiebrief te sturen naar: cbouquet@eureca-rh.com . Traducteur H/F Natif Néerlandais Eureca Strasbourg, France PRÊT(E) POUR UN NOUVEAU DÉFI ? La Commission centrale pour la navigation du Rhin (CCNR) est une organisation internationale de plus de 200 ans dont le siège est à Strasbourg. Elle compte cinq États membres (Allemagne, Belgique, France, Pays-Bas et Suisse) et a pour mission principale d’assurer la sécurité et la prospérité de la navigation rhénane. La CCNR est une organisation à la pointe de l’innovation pour permettre à la flotte rhénane d’être à l’avant-garde et de faire face aux défis d’aujourd’hui: la digitalisation, le verdissement, l’automatisation, l’adaptation au changement climatique, les qualifications du personnel ou encore la position économique du secteur. Au-delà du Rhin, de nombreuses activités de la CCNR sont maintenant réalisées dans un cadre européen. Le cabinet de recrutement Eureca recherche pour cette organisation un Traducteur H/F, de langue maternelle néerlandaise , pour renforcer son équipe linguistique. Poste en CDD (durée de 4 ans) et perspective de transformation en CDI. De beaux locaux en plein cœur de Strasbourg avec possibilité de télétravail partiel . LA MISSION QUE L’ON VOUS PROPOSE Rattaché(e) à la secrétaire générale et au sein de l’équipe de traducteurs, vos missions incluent: (80% du temps) Traduction de l’allemand et du français vers le néerlandais de textes rédactionnels, techniques et parfois politiquement sensibles, dans le respect des délais, des exigences de qualité et de la terminologie en vigueur en organisant votre charge de travail avec autonomie et flexibilité; Veille sur les domaines d'activité de l’organisation ainsi que sur les nouveautés terminologiques et linguistiques et mise à jour des mémoires de traduction et glossaires; Collaboration étroite avec les auteurs sur les choix linguistiques et stylistiques; (20% du temps) Ponctuellement, interprétation simultanée de l’allemand vers le néerlandais et inversement à l’occasion de réunions, groupes de travail et entretiens interprétés se tenant au siège de l’organisation; Préparation de chaque mission d’interprétation: prise de connaissance des documents de travail, de l’ordre du jour, des support vidéo, recherche terminologique ciblée. VOUS AIMEREZ Développer une véritable expertise sectorielle, technique ou politique, au fil des textes; Bénéficier d'un accompagnement lors de votre intégration pour faciliter votre prise de poste; Evoluer dans un environnement de travail international, dynamique et stimulant. VOUS RÉUSSIREZ À CE POSTE SI Diplômé(e) d’un Master en traduction , vous avez une excellente maîtrise de l’allemand en plus de votre langue maternelle, le néerlandais. Une bonne maîtrise du français (B2 – C1) est un atout; Idéalement, vous êtes diplômé(e) d’un Master en interprétation avec l’allemand et le néerlandais comme langues de travail ; Vous bénéficiez d’une expérience de 3 ans minimum en traduction et idéalement en interprétation; Organisé(e), vous êtes rigoureux(se) et vous appréciez le travail en équipe. Mais avant tout, vous avez la passion du travail bien fait! VOS AVANTAGES Un contrat de 4 ans avec une possibilité de conversion en CDI à l’issue de ces 4 années; Une rémunération nette d’impôts; Une bonne couverture santé et prévoyance; Une semaine de travail de 38 heures, 2 jours de télétravail par semaine, 30 jours de congés par an. Postulez en envoyant votre CV et LM à: cbouquet@eureca-rh.com . Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying. Share this Job

item.description: Communications and External Relations Officer CEPOL - European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Training Budapest, Hungary € 50,000 - € 69,999 per year Job Summary Under the supervision of the Head of Unit, the Communications and External Relations officer acts as a team leader for COMMs and RELEX teams. He/she is responsible for the development and implementation of CEPOL's communications sub-strategy as well as CEPOL's external relations strategy. He/she is responsible for the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of communication activities internally and externally, in line with the Agency's communications sub-strategy, and for CEPOL's external action, including Working Arrangements, cooperation with JHA Agencies and international organisations, relations with EU Member States and third countries, and support to CEPOL management for high-level meetings and institutional engagements. The post also includes steering, the activities of the Brussels Liaison Office. Frequent short-term missions within and outside the EU are required. Key accountabilities Develop and implement CEPOL's communications sub-strategy and external relations strategy in an integrated manner, ensuring consistency between the Agency's public messaging and its institutional/diplomatic engagement; contribute to the implementation of the CEPOL Strategy overall, including through joint stakeholder mapping. Maintain relations with press, media, and other key external partners; draft and update Working Arrangements. Act as single point of contact (SPOC) for EU Member States, EU institutions, and relevant authorities in non-EU countries; support CEPOL in strengthening ties with other EU Agencies, particularly within the JHA field (including representing CEPOL in the JHA Agencies' Network). Oversee website and social media management and the development/production of CEPOL communications materials, ensuring alignment with the Agency's brand identity and coordination with external relations messaging and institutional engagements. Oversee the intranet landing page and maintain the electronic archive of dossiers. Draft analytical and periodical reports, correspondence, briefing notes, and communications materials, in support of both public communication and institutional/diplomatic engagement. Contribute to planning, coordination, and execution of CEPOL events and high-level engagements, integrating both communications (visibility, media) and external-relations (institutional, protocol) dimensions. Monitor the activities of the Brussels Liaison Office and provide back-up when needed to ensure business continuity. Manage the teams budget allocation and expenditure; oversee contracts and service providers. Manage specific projects and tools related to CEPOL's external action and communications. Coordinate the staff assigned to Communications and External Relations activities. Other tasks as requested by the Line Manager. Eligibility criteria In addition, in order to be eligible the candidate must: Be a national of a Member State of the Union. Be entitled to his or her full rights as a citizen. Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the applicable laws on military service. Meet the character requirements for the duties involved. Be physically fit to perform the duties linked to the post; and Have a thorough knowledge (min. level C1) of one of the languages of the Union and a satisfactory knowledge (min. level B2) of another language of the Union. As the official language of the Agency is English one of the before mentioned languages has to be English. Education Level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma in the field of Communications, Public Relations, International Relations, Diplomacy, Political studies, Internal Security or a related field. Professional Experience In addition to the above, at least 3 years of relevant professional experience gained after obtaining the diploma or after completed the professional training with the experience linked to the training. Essential Criteria Minimum 3 years’ experience in developing and implementing integrated communications and external-relations strategies. Minimum 3 years’ professional experience in communications, in the public sector, including developing and managing digital and print communications, website content, social media/press and publication. Minimum 3 years’ experience in managing high-level institutional and international stakeholder relations and delivering high-level events and engagements (please describe the duration, your role, which aspects/parts you covered, etc.). Minimum 3 years’ experience in managing teams, budgets, contracts, projects and operational activities. (Please describe your exact role, budget managed, size of the team coordinated, volume of the projects, etc.). Advantageous Criteria Experience in the field of EU internal security and with cooperating with Justice and Home Affaires Agencies. Previous professional experience in protocol, including the organization and coordination of official events, high-level meetings, visits, ceremonies, and the application of institutional or diplomatic protocol procedures. Experience in drafting formal administrative reports, statements and speeches, statements, briefing notes, etc. Experience in analyzing complex political content, policies at EU level. item.description: Communications Trainee ChargeUp Europe Brussels, Belgium About ChargeUp Europe ChargeUp Europe is the voice of the electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure industry. EV charging is an innovative, fast-evolving, dynamic sector, at the forefront of the green and digital transition. Our growing membership stands for an EV charging infrastructure roll-out that starts from the consumer needs, makes EV driving convenient across borders, and promotes an open-market model supported by open standards and protocols. Function ChargeUp Europe is looking for a driven, enthusiastic junior professional for the position of Communications Trainee. The trainee will assist the ChargeUp Europe team in all communications activities and projects, including (but not limited to) helping with planning and executing events, supporting the delivery of our communications workplan, and developing content for our social media channels, while servicing members’ needs. This position will offer an opportunity to develop a broad range of communications skills, both through direct experience and by exposure to a network of seasoned communications professionals from the membership. Expected tasks 1. Social media & communications outreach: Creating engaging social media content – both short and long-form – primarily for LinkedIn, ensuring alignment with ChargeUp Europe’s visual identity; Designing clear, meaningful data visualisations and infographics to distil complex information into accessible content; Proactive outreach to stakeholders (e.g. podcast guests and hosts) and support in coordinating activities related to campaigns, podcasts and thematic series; Assisting in drafting written content for social media channels and the ChargeUp Europe website, as well as internal communication tasks and content-creation. 2. Ad-hoc assistance to the Communications Coordinator: Providing administrative and communication support, including document formatting, research, and external communications where needed; Offering ad-hoc assistance in communicating with members and handling day-to-day matters; Collecting, synthesising and analysing information from diverse sources, including data gathering, stakeholder mapping and rapid review of reports to extract key insights. 3. Creative thinking & content development: Contributing fresh, creative ideas to support communications, events and stakeholder engagement; Helping to develop concepts, visuals and messaging for campaigns, events and other formats; Keeping the ChargeUp Europe website up to date; Draft the ChargeUp Europe quarterly newsletter. 4. Logistical support for events: Providing logistical support for online and onsite events (webinars, workshops, presentations), including links, invitations and communication kits. 5. Service to the members: Responding to communications-related requests from ChargeUp Europe members and supporting member-facing activities. Please note that this list is non-exhaustive, and other tasks may be performed under this role. Required skills and competencies Master’s degree in communications or other relevant field; A basic understanding of the European policy landscape and EU institutions; Excellent writing skills in English; Interest in e-mobility; Good interpersonal and organisational skills; Experience in writing for social media, particularly LinkedIn; Experience with Canva. Our offer Targeted start date: asap. Duration: until July 2027. Contract type: CIP (la convention d’immersion professionnelle), full time, based in Brussels (flexible hybrid working regime) Renumeration: per CIP requirements Hiring process Interested candidates should send their application in English by 2 November 2026 COB at the latest to secretariat@chargeupeurope.eu , mentioning “Communications trainee” in the subject line. Please note that interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis: applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as the search will be stopped once a suitable candidate has been identified. The application should include: a CV; a cover letter, not written by AI. The cover should not be a repetition of your resume, but a document of maximum 2 pages covering the 4 questions below: What is your motivation for joining ChargeUp Europe; Tell us about a piece of content you made (post, video, newsletter, flyer…) that didn't land the way you hoped. What do you think went wrong, and what would you change? (Include a link or screenshot.); Find an organization similar to ours that does communications better. Show us one example and explain why it works; Pick one of our Linkedln posts from the 4 weeks. What would you keep, and what would you have done differently? a selection of 3 writing examples, preferably across channels/formats; a canva visual you developed. Please note that ChargeUp Europe will not consider applications that are not complete. ChargeUp Europe values diversity and encourages applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews. Please note that applicants must be authorised to work in the EU. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying. Share this Job

item.description: Campaign Director EJF - Environmental Justice Foundation Brussels, London or Berlin Contract: Three years. Hybrid working arrangements are in place Salary range: Dependent upon experience and location Applications: Please apply by 3 November 2026 About the Environmental Justice Foundation The Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) exists to protect the natural world and uphold our fundamental human right to a secure environment. We work at the frontlines of environmental injustice, alongside communities most affected by climate breakdown, biodiversity loss, and exploitation - transforming evidence into action, and injustice into lasting change. EJF is a global non-profit driven by a powerful belief: that environmental protection and human rights are inseparable. Through courageous field investigations, rigorous research, and strategic international advocacy, we expose environmental crime, challenge impunity, and catalyse systemic reform. Our work delivers real-world impact, shaping policy, strengthening governance, protecting vital ecosystems, and defending those who risk their lives to safeguard them. Our campaigns span four deeply interconnected areas: oceans, climate, forests and wetlands, and the training, protection, and empowerment of environmental defenders and journalists. From illegal fishing and forced labour to deforestation, land grabs, and climate displacement, we confront some of the most complex and urgent crises of our time - always with a focus on accountability, equity, and durable solutions. EJF is an international organisation with a diverse team working across four continents, united by a shared ambition: to protect people by protecting the planet. We are bold, evidence-led, and impact-driven. We speak truth to power - and we build pathways to a fairer, more resilient future. Join Us. About the role Over the next three years, Europe will make critical decisions that will shape the future of its seas and the global ocean for decades. During this decisive policy cycle, multiple foundational frameworks will be introduced, some might be reviewed. This is occurring amid rising political pressure for deregulation: weakening EU environmental protections would not only harm marine ecosystems and fish populations, but it would also threaten coastal livelihoods and undermine the EU’s credibility as a global standard-setter in ocean governance. This situation highlights the urgent need to reframe the public debate and policies around sustainability and low-impact fishers to achieve economic resilience, climate stability, and social equity, which are foundational to a sustainable future for Europe and beyond. EJF is working with close partners to lead a campaign to both defend and secure a robust, fit-for-purpose EU regulatory regime that protects marine ecosystems and restores biodiversity while finally ensuring a more equitable and sustainable fishing sector and putting an end to the marginalisation of small-scale fishers. Our vision is of thriving seas and thriving coastal communities going hand in hand, where a healthy ocean is the bedrock of sustainable livelihoods, jobs, and long-term economic prosperity. It is this inseparable link that will drive our engagement. The Campaign Director will lead the implementation of this flagship campaign, combining deep institutional knowledge, strategic influence, and outstanding communication skills with the credibility and networks necessary to operate at the highest levels of European policymaking. Key responsibilities The Campaign Director will: Lead a flagship EU campaign strategy to defend and secure strong, science-based and fair ocean policies during the current European policy cycle; Co-develop and co-execute high-impact advocacy plans targeting the European Commission, European Parliament, Council of the EU, and Member State governments, ensuring timely influence at key political moments; Establish and maintain close relationships and constructive collaborations with NGOs, fishers’ organisations, academics, legal experts and other allies to maximise influence and alignment; Coordinate the delivery of work across team members across the coalition to deliver the campaign; Build and maintain senior-level political relationships with policymakers, advisers, diplomats, regulators and other decision-makers to advance campaign objectives; Lead debate framing and messaging that position healthy seas, biodiversity restoration and thriving coastal communities as mutually reinforcing priorities; Represent, as needed and appropriate, the campaign externally in high-level meetings, conferences, roundtables, media opportunities and stakeholder forums with authority and credibility; Identify political opportunities and risks, providing strategic intelligence and recommendations to adapt campaign tactics in a fast-moving policy environment; Secure measurable policy outcomes, tracking progress against campaign goals and working with the collaboration to adjust strategies to maximise impact; Ensure strong delivery, accountability and value for money; Contribute to donor engagement, including helping shape proposals, reporting on impact and supporting opportunities. Person specification Essential: You will have sharp political insight and strategic vision, be results-driven, demonstrate strong initiative, have credibility in senior policy environments, and be able to represent the campaign with authority and professionalism. This should include the ability to work across governments, NGOs and industry; Outstanding communicator : A persuasive and authoritative communicator capable of engaging senior policymakers, partners, and public audiences. item.description: Policy Analyst on Gender Equality (6-month-long Determinate Contract Aimed at Continuation with Indeterminate Contract) FEPS - Foundation for European Progressive Studies Brussels, Belgium € 4.500 per month gross Deadline for Applications: Monday, November 23 rd 2026 noon CET The Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS – www.feps-europe.eu ) is currently looking for one Policy Analyst for a thematic field: Gender Equality . The successful candidate is to join the FEPS Team based in Brussels from January 2027 onwards (cf. selection timetable below). FEPS is an equal opportunity employer, committed to enhancing fairness and to achieving workplace diversity. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all suitably qualified candidates, irrespective of gender, disability, marital or parental status, racial, ethnic or social origin, colour, religion, belief, or sexual orientation. About FEPS: The Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) is the think tank of the progressive political family at the EU level. Our mission is to develop innovative research, policy advice, training and debates to inspire and inform socialist and social democratic politics and policies across Europe. FEPS operates as hub for thinking to facilitate the emergence of progressive answers to the challenges that Europe faces today. FEPS works in close partnership with its members and partners, forging connections and boosting coherence among stakeholders from the world of politics, academia and civil society at local, regional, national, European and global levels. Today FEPS benefits from a network of 76 member organisations. Among these, 40 are full members, 31 have observer status and 5 are ex-officio members. In addition to this network of organisations that are active in the promotion of progressive values, FEPS also has an extensive network of partners, including renowned universities, scholars, policymakers and activists. FEPS’ ambition is to undertake intellectual reflection for the benefit of the progressive movement, and to promote the founding principles of the EU – freedom, equality, solidarity, democracy, respect of human rights, fundamental freedoms, human dignity, and the rule of law. Reporting Line: FEPS’ Policy Analysts report daily to the delegate of the Secretary General (i.e. the Director or Head of Programme appointed to supervise the thematic field in question). Mission of the Role: The mission of the Policy Analyst is to substantiate FEPS’ work on Gender Equality. S.he will embody FEPS’ internal expertise in the field (including feminism, anti-discrimination policies, equal opportunity, social investment, demography etc.). To do so, the Policy Analyst will design, steer and implement a coherent portfolio of FEPS (co-)funded projects (including its development and consolidation) aimed at impacting policies, political debates and/or public awareness related to the EU’s approach to Gender Equality. The ideal candidate will have the following profile: At least an MA or MSc degree in a relevant field. A PhD will be considered a relevant asset and account to the years of professional experience; Knowledge and interest for EU affairs and political sensitivity; At least 5 years professional experience in a field connected to Gender Equality; Proven expertise in quantitative and qualitative research, data analyses and surveys design; Capacity to follow developments at international, European, national, regional and local levels, and analyse relevant trends across political, economic and social dimensions; Experience in designing, overseeing and managing multi-stakeholders’ projects; Written and oral proficiency in English and in a second European language. Any additional European language will be considered an asset; Proven ability to draft analysis, research and policy recommendations; A strong set of soft skills, with specific reference to: Innovative and out-of-the-box thinking; High organisational and time-management skills; Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; Advanced interpersonal and social skills; Exceptional team player with the ability to contribute positively to a team; Ability to work under pressure and tight deadlines. Readiness to travel and adapt to flexible working hours. Employment conditions: The position is to be filled out as from January 2027 onwards. The position is to be filled out January 2027; The duration of the contract will be 6 months (potentially renewable in the form of an indeterminate contract); The fixed starting monthly gross salary will be 4.500 EUR; The workplace will be Brussels (Belgium); Applicants must be able to work and reside in Belgium; As FEPS is registered in Belgium, the contract will be under Belgian law. Applications’ composition and deadline: Applications are to be done online by Monday the 23 rd of November 2026 at noon CET . Your application is to include: A cover letter outlining your motivation for the post and your understanding of progressive values (maximum 2 pages); A detailed CV without picture (possibly in Europass format); A sample of work authored in the thematic field covered by the present notice (links or attached); The name of 2 referees with the related contact details. Applications not respecting the completion and submission instructions will not be considered. Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage for the purpose of applying with FEPS: Although specifically drafted for the purpose of research and writing activities, FEPS’ general approach and principles for the usage of Artificial Intelligence apply: https://feps-europe.eu/responsible-use-of-ai-in-research-and-writing-activities/ : Applicants wishing to use AI for the purpose of preparing their application are free to do so. By way of the online application forms (dedicated tick boxes and fields are foreseen in this respect) : All applicants will be requested to declare whether they used AI or not; All documents submitted for the purpose of all applications will be scanned and reviewed to check for the use of AI tools; If an applicant declares that AI has not been used but that the review raises any doubt about an undeclared use of AI, the related application will be eliminated; Applicants declaring having used AI for the purpose of preparing their application: Must declare how and for which of the submitted documents AI was used; Must upload the Markdown (MD) file(s) containing the prompts and AI conversations used to generate the related documents. Submitted MD file(s) will be used for the purpose of crosschecking (1) consistency with FEPS’ AI approach and principles and (2) the applicant’s AI literacy. Please note that the usage of AI is hereby not encouraged. The fact of using AI or not is not an assessment criteria as such. Transparency about its usage is and, in the case of usage, AI literacy will be. The tentative selection timetable is the following: Deadline for submission of complete applications: Monday 23.11.2026 noon CET ; Eligibility check and first assessment of written applications: This will result in a shortlist of no more than 6 candidates who will be invited for the subsequent step. First round of interviews of candidates & short written test between 30.11.2026 and 04.12.2026: This will result in a shortlist of no more than 3 candidates who will be invited for the subsequent step. Second interview of shortlisted candidates: early January 2027; Communication of the final results to candidates: by the end of January 2027. During the entire selection procedure, FEPS is absolutely committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background. We value diversity and lived experience, and acknowledge the underrepresentation of people from certain backgrounds. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential. The equal opportunity principle encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their gender, sexual orientation, origins or disabilities. item.title: CEB Internship Programme 2027
item.description: CEB Internship Programme 2027 CEB - Council of Europe Development Bank Paris, France € 1,800 per month The Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) offers ten internships in Paris for students in their final year of higher education and recent graduates. From analysing financial risk to assessing social investment, the programme gives you the chance to apply what you’ve studied to the work of a bank with a social mandate. Working with colleagues from different backgrounds, you’ll contribute to assignments in your chosen team and develop skills through research, analysis, drafting or technical work. The CEB finances projects in areas such as education, health and affordable housing, with a focus on vulnerable people. Explore the ten internships Each description outlines the work and the profile sought. The shared eligibility criteria follow the ten roles; role-specific qualifications and skills also apply. Read the full vacancy before applying. 1. Business Process and AI Innovation In the Loans & Social Development Directorate, you’ll explore where AI can make everyday work easier. That starts with understanding how colleagues take a project from an initial idea through appraisal, monitoring and completion. Your work could take you from mapping a process to testing an AI-assisted workflow with approved tools such as Microsoft Copilot. You’ll also prepare guidance, prompt repositories and training materials, learning how to turn an operational need into something colleagues can use. Your profile: Studies in business administration, information systems, business analytics, digital transformation, data science, AI, computer science, engineering, public administration, economics or a related field. You’ll need analytical and drafting skills, knowledge of Microsoft 365 and an interest in AI. Familiarity with process modelling, Copilot or automation tools is an advantage. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Business-process-and-AI-innovation-Stagiaire-processus-m%C3%A9tier-et-de-l%26apos%3Binnovation-IA/1374188955/ . 2. Corporate Responsibility The CEB is preparing its first sustainability report aligned with ISSB standards for publication in 2027. In the Corporate Responsibility & ESG Reporting Unit, you could contribute to that work alongside the ESG Officer and ESG Data Analyst. You’ll help with sustainability disclosures, support engagement with ESG rating agencies and follow progress on aligning internal operations with the Paris Agreement. Tracking reporting developments and writing website and intranet content will give you practical experience of how sustainability information is assembled and explained. Your profile: Studies in sustainability management or related fields such as finance, law, economics or political science. Good drafting skills matter, as do familiarity with sustainability standards and disclosures and working knowledge of ESG ratings and risks. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Corporate-Responsibility-Stagiaire-Responsabilit%C3%A9-d%26apos%3BEntreprise/1374189655/ . 3. Corporate Services Behind the CEB’s lending work are the people and services that keep the Bank running. This role gives you a view across HR, IT, and facilities and travel management, working directly with the Corporate Services Director on shared priorities. You might be bringing together project and budget updates, preparing a briefing or following up on actions agreed by different teams. You’ll also review processes and help explore practical uses of AI and automation. These assignments offer experience in making sense of complex issues and coordinating work across the Directorate. Your profile: Studies in management, business analysis or a related field. The role calls for strong analytical and organisational skills, the ability to structure complex issues and ease working both independently and with different teams. Knowledge of Lean or Agile methods and an interest in practical AI and automation are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Corporate-Services/1374174355/ . 4. Environmental and Social Sustainability and Climate Change A project’s environmental and social effects matter to a financing decision. In the Environmental and Social Sustainability Unit, you’ll help examine those effects and the climate risks and opportunities that come with them. The work includes screening risks, reviewing borrower information and legislation, and contributing to safeguards assessments. You’ll also support climate assessments covering Paris Agreement alignment and opportunities for adaptation or mitigation. Working through these questions with technical specialists offers a practical introduction to project due diligence and the methods behind it. Your profile: Studies in social studies, political sciences, community development, planning, applied economics, environmental sciences or a related discipline. Strong analysis and clear technical writing are essential, together with teamwork and the ability to manage changing deadlines. Courses on climate risks and resilience are an asset. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Environmental-and-Social-Sustainability-Climate-Change/1374177755/ . 5. Evaluation What did a development project achieve, and what could the next one do better? In the Office of Independent Evaluation, you’ll help gather and examine the evidence behind its findings. Expect to work with project and sector literature, analyse information, contribute to stakeholder interviews and prepare charts for evaluation outputs. You’ll also help with meetings and knowledge-sharing events. These assignments offer practice in research and presenting evidence, while showing you how independent evaluation informs learning and accountability. Your profile: Studies in evaluation, development studies, economics, social or political sciences, urban or environmental studies, business administration and international affairs. You should be interested in social, economic and environmental issues and highly proficient in MS Office, including Excel and PowerPoint. Knowledge of evaluation methods, additional analysis software and relevant professional or voluntary experience are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Evaluation/1374174555/ . 6. Legal Administrative Issues Staff rules, procurement and institutional privileges all raise legal questions for an international organisation. In the Office of the General Counsel’s Administrative Issues Unit, you’ll see how those questions are handled, working under experienced legal colleagues. You may assist with research on staff rules and disputes, privileges and immunities, or service contracts and procurement. Other assignments can include presentations and knowledge tools, including AI solutions for corporate contract management. It’s an opportunity to apply legal research and drafting to institutional matters with supervision. Your profile: Studies in law, focused on International Administrative Law, Law of International Organisations, or International or European Law. You’ll need accurate legal analysis, advising and drafting skills, the ability to manage deadlines and sound knowledge of IT and electronic document management tools. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Administrative-Issues/1374174855/ . 7. Long Term Investments and Liquidity If you enjoy finding meaning in financial data, this role offers a way to put that interest to work. You’ll be based in the Treasury & Asset and Liability Management Division, collaborating with colleagues in the CEB’s Dealing Room. Historical data analysis, capital markets notes and internal financial reports are all part of the work. You’ll also help develop dashboards covering financial and environmental, social and governance factors. It’s a practical setting for your data and coding skills, with exposure to treasury activities at a development bank. Your profile: Studies in finance, engineering, statistical and actuarial sciences, mathematics, banking or a related field. Strong analysis and critical thinking are important, supported by strong computer skills, particularly Excel including VBA coding or other coding languages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Long-Term-Investments-%26-Liquidity/1374177555/ . 8. Market Risk Risk models need calculations that stand up to scrutiny. In the Market Risk and Capital Management Unit, you’ll work on quantitative questions with colleagues across Risk & Control, Finance and IT. Assignments include developing checks for derivatives pricing curves and an in-house Credit Valuation Adjustment tool. You’ll analyse capital, provisioning and liquidity stress-testing models, and explore AI for model analysis, documentation and automation. You’ll get practice testing models and explaining what the findings mean. Your profile: Studies in quantitative finance, financial or applied mathematics, statistics, data science, computer science, engineering or an equivalent quantitative discipline. It requires strong quantitative and problem-solving skills, very good knowledge of at least one programming language, preferably Python or R, and an interest in risk modelling. VBA, SQL, Git or AI-assisted development tools are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Market-Risk-Stagiaire-Risque-de-March%C3%A9/1374189555/ . 9. Projects How does an idea for a school, hospital or affordable housing project become a financing proposal? In the Projects Division of Loans & Social Development, you’ll help a Country Manager with the research, analysis and documents that move proposals forward. You’ll support project identification and appraisal, help prepare Framework Loan Agreements and draft material for reports and presentation
